fleet_learning.title: Learning from the fleet ledger
fleet_learning.summary: Distilled from 71879 rows of the mega-batch ledger (71807 completed evaluations); every relationship carries measured fit quality, never assertion.
highlights: Across 23948 wing polars, higher aspect ratio raises L/D: about +1.89 in L/D per unit of aspect ratio, and the fit explains 93 percent of the variance (r2 = 0.93). That is a strong relationship, measured, not assumed.
The induced-drag rows imply a span efficiency near 1.02 (spread 0.02 over 23948 polars), pulled straight from cl and cdi.
Best wing seen so far: L/D 47.1 at aspect ratio 16.0 and sweep 16.9 deg (ledger row 40402).
Over 23899 cylinder solves in the steady-laminar band, Cd falls with Re with a log-log slope of -0.43 (r2 = 1.00), consistent with laminar drag theory.
100 percent of the 23899 cylinder solves converged to residual tolerance.
Across 23960 reduced-order valve evaluations, wider opening angles cut cycle-weighted loss (slope -148.6 Pa per degree, r2 = 0.75); the lowest loss seen is 1267 Pa at 85.0 deg (ledger row 11072).
Reliability: 72 of 71879 attempted evaluations failed (0 percent); every failure stays in the ledger and counts against the fleet.
All of the above rests on 71807 completed evaluations in the fleet ledger; nothing here is asserted without a row behind it.

credentials.reason: within 5% of Hoerner, Fluid-Dynamic Drag (1965), Ch. 3 (rectangular and cubic blocks), Cd 1.05 (band ±15%), but the grid-refinement study for this setup came back inconclusive; not enough to call it validated

credentials.name: cylinder
credentials.source: Hoerner, Fluid-Dynamic Drag (1965), Ch. 3 (finite-aspect cylinders in crossflow)
credentials.reason:
measured Cd 0.546 matches the supercritical / fully-turbulent regime (Cd ~0.5, Hoerner (1965), supercritical branch below the subcritical 0.74), not the subcritical crossflow, free-end relief reference Cd 0.74; fully-turbulent steady RANS under-predicts the subcritical base drag of the finite cylinder, landing near the supercritical branch rather than the subcritical reference
; no like-for-like comparison available

credentials.name: flat_plate
credentials.source: thin-airfoil / finite-wing theory; consistent with Hoerner, Fluid-Dynamic Drag, lifting surfaces
credentials.reason: within 8% of thin-airfoil / finite-wing theory; consistent with Hoerner, Fluid-Dynamic Drag, lifting surfaces, Cd 0.03 (band ±35%), but that reference is itself a low-confidence estimate, not a settled measurement; not enough to call it validated

credentials.name: sphere
credentials.source: Achenbach 1972, J. Fluid Mech. 54:565; consistent with Schlichting, Boundary-Layer Theory
credentials.reason:
measured Cd 0.095 matches the supercritical (post-drag-crisis) regime (Cd ~0.09, Achenbach 1972 (supercritical branch, Cd ~ 0.07-0.10)), not the subcritical (laminar separation, wide wake) reference Cd 0.47; steady fully-turbulent RANS delays boundary-layer separation and reproduces the post-drag-crisis wake, so the coefficient reads supercritical even when the solve Reynolds number is subcritical
; no like-for-like comparison available
